newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean won closes lower on import deals.
newsitem.headline: South Korean won closes lower on import deals.

text.p: The won closed lower against the dollar on Wednesday on dollar buying for import deals due this week and early next week, dealers said.
Wednesday was the last trading day of the week as the market will be closed during the September 26-28 Korean Thanksgiving holidays and reopen on Monday.
The won closed at 821.10, down from the day's opening rate of 820.60. The currency ranged from 820.40 to 822.00.
"Dollar buying was steady throughout the day as a large number of import deals are scheduled early next week," said a dealer at Chase Manhattan Bank.
Dealers said the 822 won level was seen as a strong resistance level and traders refrained from actively buying the U.S. unit over the level.
"Traders saw the dollar weakening early next month when a huge amount of dollar supply is expected after the foreign shareholding limit is raised," said a local bank dealer.
The foreign stock ownership limit is due to be raised to 20 percent on October 1 from 18 percent at present.
Dealers saw a 820.00-823.00 range on Monday, with the base mid-rate at around 821.10. The won's mid-rate was pegged at 820.60 on Wednesday. --YOO CHOON-SIK (822) 727 5646
